objective: Preserve the provider-side error from a completed Colab runtime-creation operation so physical render qualification failures are diagnosable instead of being collapsed into a generic missing-runtime-response error.

rulesConsidered: Notebook adapters remain bounded provider adapters and do not gain F06 worker authority.
Physical notebook qualification requires real runtime execution and physical artifact evidence.
Provider error evidence must be retained without persisting credentials or runtime proxy tokens.

notes: No credentials were added or persisted.
Only provider operation code/message/details are surfaced; runtime proxy tokens remain in process memory.
Provider error details are truncated to a bounded 2000-character representation.

changes: Colab provision now checks completed-operation error payloads before requiring response.name.
Provider error code, message, and bounded details are included in the thrown diagnostic.
The generic missing-response error now includes the operation name.
Added a deterministic regression test for a completed Colab operation with a RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error.

failureEvidence.phase: runtime creation operation completion before Jupyter execution
failureEvidence.existingSuccessfulProof: A prior live T4 create/delete control-plane run succeeded.

verificationPlan: Pass Team Change Gate, OKF Governance, and repository CI.
Run the Colab physical qualification probe once the diagnostic code is merged.
Use the surfaced provider operation error to distinguish capacity/quota from request-contract failures.
Do not mark Colab QUALIFIED unless the physical MP4, SHA-256, byte length, and MP4 signature checks pass.
notes: The local RenderFabric background typecheck failure was inspected against current main and is not introduced by this Colab diagnostic change.
This PR intentionally does not change Colab runtime creation semantics; it improves error observability.
